requirements.requirement: Keep a persistent host firewall enabled on node1 across restart.
requirements.summary: firewalld was active and enabled with matching runtime and permanent policy before restart. After an acknowledged restart and changed boot ID, firewalld recovered active and enabled with the same policy and kernel rules.

requirements.requirement: Permit inbound SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections.
requirements.summary: Final IPv4 and IPv6 rules explicitly accept TCP/22 and TCP/8080 and reject other inbound traffic. Bounded tests with listeners showed TCP/8080 accepted and TCP/8081 rejected both before and after restart; SSH remained listening and usable after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 from baseline through the final post-restart observation. The implementation used the already-installed RHEL 7 firewalld/iptables stack, with no package or platform replacement shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The firewall policy and connection behavior were directly verified before and after a genuine node restart, and the provider-wide restart protocol is complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot observations. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out in both lifecycle snapshots, so package integrity was not independently confirmed.
Connection behavior was directly exercised over IPv4; IPv6 enforcement is supported by directly observed kernel rules but was not separately traffic-tested.
The broad process-match cleanup command self-terminated, and the evidence cannot determine whether it briefly affected any unrelated matching process.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing firewall work, reboot, and temporary network/listener tests had clear task or evidence roles. Test listeners, namespaces, and interfaces were restored, and no failed units or unwanted listeners remained. The unnecessary retained mutations were eight executor-created temporary evidence files: /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log from the restart command; three pre-restart firewall-test logs/error files; and three post-restart firewall-test logs/error files. These remained after completion despite being low-risk and bounded. The broad corrective pkill command self-terminated; the trace does not establish that it affected unrelated processes, and final health was clean.
